pillar_reactions.evidence: Internal call between closer and setter. No pillars presented and no prospect present.

unmet_demand.want: A way to sell to a prospect who wants the programme but cannot physically start yet — relayed second-hand about a prospect referred to as Montana, whose back was 'blown out' at the time of the call
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The offer is a six-month commitment beginning immediately, with no deferred start, no pause, and no rehabilitation-first pathway. The closer's read was that the prospect 'definitely needs to rest first', so he withheld the pitch entirely and booked a second call for the following Thursday rather than sell something the prospect could not use. That is a sound decision and it left the company with nothing to offer someone with high intent and a temporary physical barrier. The same shape appears in the existing Tyron Giuliani assessment.

unmet_demand.want: Reliable financial qualification before a prospect reaches a $6,000 closing call
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The current method is a job-title lookup in ChatGPT — 'when I put that into ChatGPT, it said he was probably making around 75k' for a commercial diver, and 'I once again chat GPT'd, like, estimated salary for a five-year firefighter, and it said that would be around 60k'. Estimated occupational salary says nothing about disposable income, debt, dependants or liquidity, which is precisely what decided most of the calls in this batch: a man on over six figures with zero available cash, an accountant with two mortgages and a $1,000/month ceiling, a veteran on disability with five children, and a retired teacher expecting to pay $30 a month. This is a process gap rather than a product one, and it is recorded here because it is stated explicitly.
